content:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: kv cache memory growth detected on gpu-pool-phi-3 (p3.8xlarge). 95th p99 latency spike and node OOMs reported. auto-escalation -> incidents channel.
alex: saw repeated CUDA OOMs and huge fragmentation in /var/log/inference/kv_allocator.log, starting ~23:02 UTC.
maria: confirming — stack shows `malloc failed` from pytorch cuda allocator. attaching snippet: ```
E pytorch.cuda: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 13.20 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 13.50 GiB reserved)
```
charlie: @alex @maria any recent batch-config or kv cache changes?
alex: yes, a config push two hours ago increased `continuous_batching.max_window` to 300 and enabled `cache.prefix_sharing` experiment for perf.
maria: that matches timeline. suspect combination: larger windows + prefix cache = unbounded KV growth + allocator fragmentation.
sam: starting mitigation checklist from runbook: 1) throttle continuous batching 2) disable prefix_sharing 3) trigger KV compaction 4) divert traffic if unstable. I'll take action.
charlie: +1. Put a canary hold: reduce to `max_window=100` first.
sam: running: `redwoodctl set-config inference.continuous_batching.max_window=100 --pool gpu-pool-phi-3` — applied.
alex: pushing disable flag: `redwoodctl set-feature cache.prefix_sharing=false --env prod --pool gpu-pool-phi-3`
deploy-bot: config change applied by sam @ 23:12 UTC — 3 nodes updated, 2 pending.
maria: checking metrics — memory growth rate slowed but fragmentation remains; p99 latencies still elevated.
nina: clients reporting errors: 14% 5xx across hosted endpoints hitting phi-3. logging ticket numbers in status page.
charlie: can we trigger a background compaction process? runbook suggests `kv-tool compact --pool phi-3 --target=aggressive`
sam: executed `kv-tool compact --pool phi-3 --target=aggressive` at 23:18 UTC.
alex: compaction logs show reclaimed ~6 GB on node-2 but node-0 still has high reserved chunks; I think allocator arenas are fragmented.
maria: short-term binary workaround: enable `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` for the runtime to reduce fragmentation. Recommend rolling to one node to test.
charlie: @maria please prod one node with env change via `pm apply-env` to verify.
maria: applied on node-0 only. monitoring.
(2m later)
maria: env tweak reduced small-allocation scatter but p99 mem reserved still high. fragmentation not fully resolved.
sam: escalate to infra: consider LD_PRELOAD jemalloc and changing `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` not enough. we might need allocator patch.
alex: we have a candidate hotfix branch that adjusts arena reslicing and disables lazy-split for large contiguous reservations. I'll open a canary hotpatch.
charlie: given customer impact, divert 30% traffic away from phi-3 to phi-1/phi-2. runbook step: create routing override.
sam: `redwoodctl route adjust --from phi-3 --to phi-1 --percent 30` — applied.
nina: customer-impact update: ~12 customers on paid plans saw degraded responses; posted to status.redwood.ai with ETA 1h.
(10m later)
alex: hotpatch branch built and smoke-tested in staging. preparing canary deploy to one node in phi-3.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started by alex @ 23:43 UTC -> phi-3-node-1.
maria: canary node shows lowered reserved memory and removed `malloc` spikes. running longer soak. logs: `allocator: reslice success, freed contiguous ranges`.
charlie: if canary stays green for 15m, roll to the pool.
(15m later)
deploy-bot: canary healthy 15m. rolling patch to remaining phi-3 nodes.
sam: rolling completed @ 00:10 UTC.
alex: post-roll metrics: memory reclaimed across nodes, p99 latency back to baseline, error rate down to <1%.
nina: updating status page: incident mitigated, partial rollback of batch/config changes, initiating postmortem.
charlie: action items for postmortem: 1) revert `continuous_batching.max_window` increase until we have guardrails 2) add KV cache growth alarm tied to reserved memory not just allocated 3) add allocator-tuning runbook for pytorch cuda edge-cases 4) test jemalloc vs default answers 5) create canary gating for cache.prefix_sharing.
maria: I'll own item 1 and 5. alex will take #4 and #3. sam will draft the customer-impact timeline.
alex: note: also queue a kernel-level nudge to the `gpu-pool` autoscaler to prefer draining nodes with highest fragmentation during compactions.
charlie: thanks team. filing incident doc and assigning P0 postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident closed: mitigation verified @ 00:25 UTC. Pager duty auto-resolve.
